subject: dr117-ee-gate-naming.v1

verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 3 SHOULD-FIX. The rule is not discretionary, so the verdict is REJECT.
acceptanceGrade: REJECT-ON-CUSTODY-COMPLETENESS. The substance is right and I say so plainly: every attack the prompt names is refuted, all nine verbatim quotations are byte-exact, and the three class-to-gate placements are correct. What fails is that this successor drops three custody elements its own accepted predecessor carries — and carries specifically because it repaired findings from earlier turns of this same naming lineage.

shouldFix.title: No condition-4 effect statement, which is the exact defect that made me REJECT gate-harness-naming.v5
shouldFix.finding: The artifact states requiredNowUnchanged 24 but says nothing about what recording it would do to condition 4. Its predecessor carries condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded for precisely this reason: v6's own basedOn.relation records 'Claude REJECT 0/1 CLAUDE-GHN-V5-SF1. This successor states the condition-4 effect of recording this naming: zero. Condition 4 stays MET on the naming half.' The successor drops the repair and restores the gap.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: G09, G14 and G16 are all inside the required-now 24 and all already name a recorded identifier, so adding rider classes moves the naming half by zero and condition 4 stays MET at 24 of 24. That is the right answer, and it is exactly the answer an unstated effect lets a later drafter get wrong in the other direction — a naming act that looks like naming progress is how a required-gate denominator gets misreported.
shouldFix.repair: Add a condition4Effect field stating that recording this naming moves the condition-4 naming half by zero, that condition 4 stays MET at 24 of 24 required gates naming a recorded identifier and 28 of 28 owners named, and that MET is not QUALIFIED.

shouldFix.title: No COORD digest and no remeasurement clause, both of which landed in the predecessor as repairs to my own earlier finding
shouldFix.finding: The artifact pins file 08 and HEAD but not COORD, and carries no remeasurement clause. v6 carries both — COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md sits in its recordedInputs map and its remeasurementClause spells out the PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT exception for append-only COORD growth and duplicate-heading hygiene — and v6's findingDisposition records both as the landing sites of CLAUDE-GHN-V4-SF1.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: This is not hypothetical here. COORD has already moved twice since the pinned file-08 state, by the D-156 adoption and then the duplicate-heading hygiene commit that is this artifact's own HEAD. A naming candidate with no COORD pin and no remeasurement clause gives a later recorder no stated way to tell benign append-only growth from a scope-affecting move, which is the whole purpose the clause was added to serve.
shouldFix.repair: Add COORD at f87934e2 to a recordedInputs map alongside the pins already present, and copy v6's remeasurement clause with this artifact's operands substituted.

shouldFix.title: The contracts that supply the naming's authority are cited by name without digests
shouldFix.finding: All three executes fields cite preview-product-boundary-successor.v5 as the source of the class law, and the G16 executes additionally cites monorepo-ci-contract.v16 for IR-1..IR-4 / G16-12. Neither is pinned. The artifact pins its predecessor, the join and file 08, so the omission is selective rather than a uniform house style, and the predecessor pins its own product law — provider-only-output-contract.v3 — with a digest.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The join is pinned but the join only measures which classes are capable of riding. What each class actually asserts — EE-6b as disclosure rather than prevention, EE-7e as IR-1..IR-4 / G16-12 — comes from v5 and from the monorepo contract. Those are the bytes a later recorder must be able to re-measure, and they are the two this artifact leaves unpinned. Both are correct today: v5 is at 5face6a9 and monorepo-ci-contract.v16 at 67ca5016, matching v5's own pin. Recording the naming without pinning them is what makes a future silent move undetectable.
shouldFix.repair: Add preview-product-boundary-successor.v5 at 5face6a9 and monorepo-ci-contract.v16 at 67ca5016 to the same recordedInputs map.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The artifact does not carry v6's whatNamingIs / whatNamingIsNot, inheritedRecitals or findingDisposition blocks
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: Those serve v6's much wider scope — twenty-two gates and a chain of inherited D-086-era recitals. This candidate amends three executes fields, and its commission plus per-gate doesNotClaim already carry the naming-is-not-execution law. Requiring the full predecessor shape for a three-gate amendment would be template worship, not review.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Grading SF1 through SF3 as a single bundled finding
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: Codex was right to charge me on bundling at D-140 turn 2. These are three distinct omissions with three distinct repairs, so they are listed separately even though one recordedInputs map would carry two of them.

A v2 that adds a condition4Effect field, a recordedInputs map carrying COORD, v5 and monorepo-ci-contract.v16, and v6's remeasurement clause would on this review's evidence reach 0 and 0.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 3 SHOULD-FIX. The substance is right and should not be relitigated in v2. All nine verbatim quotations — claim, harness and owner for G09, G14 and G16 — are byte-exact against live file 08, including the G16 owner parenthetical an earlier turn of this lineage once dropped. The three placements match both the pinned join's owedLater instructions and v5's existingGate fields, no leftover class appears in any nowNames, required-now is stated unchanged at 24 against the live cell, and every SATISFIED, Class A, implementation and QUALIFIED occurrence is a refusal. On the row where I previously accepted a false enforcement claim, the EE-6b executes now says disclosure honesty and leaves demonstrated prevention at DR-128, matching v5 rather than contradicting it. IR-1..IR-4 and G16-12 all exist in the live monorepo-ci-contract.v16 at the digest v5 pins. What fails is custody completeness against the artifact's own accepted predecessor, which is the same document class. Three elements v6 carries are absent, and v6's findingDisposition and basedOn.relation record all three as repairs it made to findings from earlier turns of this naming lineage. First, no condition-4 effect statement — the exact defect for which I rejected v5 as CLAUDE-GHN-V5-SF1; the true effect is zero and condition 4 stays MET at 24 of 24, and leaving it unstated is how a naming act gets mistaken for naming progress. Second, no COORD pin and no remeasurement clause, both of which landed in v6 from CLAUDE-GHN-V4-SF1; that is live rather than theoretical here, since COORD has already moved twice since the pinned file-08 state, by the D-156 adoption and by the hygiene commit that is this artifact's own HEAD. Third, the contracts supplying the naming's authority — v5 for all three classes and monorepo-ci-contract.v16 for the G16 identifiers — are cited by name with no digests, while the predecessor, join and file 08 are pinned, so the omission is selective. All three repairs are purely additive; nothing already in the artifact needs to change. One tool-side self-correction is recorded: my first row extraction failed because the live id cell reads 'DR-G09 PERMISSIONS' rather than a bare identifier, and the nine exact matches come from the corrected pass.
